message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and importance as international hubs:

| Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) | Atlanta, GA | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | Key gateway to Asia, Oceania, and Latin America; major hub for American Airlines and United. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport (ORD) | Chicago, IL | ORD | One of the busiest airports in the U.S.; major hub for United and American. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the largest single-runway airports. |
| Denver International Airport (DEN) | Denver, CO | DEN | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; hub for United and Southwest. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) | New York City, NY | JFK | Primary gateway to Europe and the Caribbean; major hub for American and Delta. |
| San Francisco International Airport (SFO) | San Francisco, CA | SFO | Major hub for United and a key gateway to Asia. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA) | Seattle, WA | SEA | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| Miami International Airport (MIA) | Miami, FL | MIA | Major hub for LATAM and a key gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) | Phoenix, AZ | PHX | Hub for American and Southwest; one of the busiest airports in the Southwest. |
| Orlando International Airport (MCO) | Orlando, FL | MCO | Major hub for Southwest; key gateway to the theme‑park tourism market. |
| Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT) | Charlotte, NC | CLT | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the fastest‑growing airports. |
| Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) | Washington, DC | IAD | Major hub for United; primary airport for the Washington metropolitan area. |
| Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) | Newark, NJ | EWR | Major hub for United; serves the New York City region. |

These airports are among the busiest in terms of passenger numbers, flight operations, and international connectivity. They serve as major hubs for airlines and are critical nodes in both domestic and global air travel networks.
